text:
omar: Quick heads-up — canary NF4/FP4 rollout in us-west-2 showing a 20-35% throughput drop on long-chat workload samples after the recent calibration tweak. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

jane: Yep, saw the same on canary-3 around 09:12. Also spotted a memory bump on the KV cache (unexpected). Reverting the calib locally helped throughput go back up.

liam: @omar what's the exact calibration change you rolled? layerwise scales or different clipping thresholds?

sasha: We switched FP4 fallback to use layerwise scale estimation (was global) and enabled the new per-token smoothing heuristics for quant. The change was intended to reduce quality regressions, not perf regressions.

nidhi: I captured a short profile from canary-3. Posting the key lines: 
```
# workload: long-chat synthetic, seq=2048, batch=4
baseline (pre-calib): tokens/s=860, avg-lat=18ms, kv-mem=3.1GB
post-calib: tokens/s=540, avg-lat=28ms, kv-mem=5.0GB
kernel switches: up +120% (more fallbacks to int8/slow-4bit kernel)
CPU sched wait spikes on batching thread: +40%
```
ryan: That kv-mem change is alarming — +1.9GB for same workload. Could be KV cache fragmentation from different kv layout due to per-layer quant params?

omar: My suspicion is kernel selection oscillation: calibration changes made some layers choose different quant kernels which have different KV layout assumptions. When that mixes across layers we might lose the shared KV compacting optimization and trigger more allocations.

jane: Also seen more small micro-batches being emitted by the batching heuristics (we had bursty input). If kernel latency varies by layer, the batching window starts to split. So throughput drops and memory goes up because more intermediate KV buffers are live.

liam: Repro steps I ran locally: 
1) checkout branch `nf4/fp4-calib-2026`
2) run `./tools/run_infer --model t5-xxl --seq 2048 --batch 4 --canary`
3) compare `perf_summary.json` before/after
I can share full perf_profile if helpful.

sasha: I pushed a quick telemetry patch to log kernel id per-layer and batching boundaries. We'll get clearer numbers from the canary traces.

nidhi: Adding the partial diff of `kernel_selection.cc` changes that look suspicious: 
```diff
- choose_kernel(global_scale)
+ choose_kernel(layer_scale, smoothing=true)
```
That change can easily nudge a layer from fast 4-bit kernel to an int8 fallback under specific activation statistics.

ryan: For mitigation, two quick experiments: 1) force kernel pinning to previous global-scale kernels (cheap revert) and 2) relax batching preemption timeout to allow slower kernels to finish within same batch. Which do we want to try first?

omar: Try kernel pinning on canary-3 first (safe, quick). If that restores throughput, we know selection is root cause. Then we can instrument the smoothing logic to avoid oscillation.

jane: Rolling kernel-pinning to canary-3 now. deploy-bot: request to canary-3 to set env `FORCE_KERNEL=legacy_global`
deploy-bot: started rollback job #2739 -> canary-3 (triggered by jane)

deploy-bot: rollback completed in ~45s, smoke tests passed.

nidhi: Post-rollback quick numbers (same synthetic sample): 
```
post-rollback: tokens/s=830, avg-lat=19ms, kv-mem=3.3GB
```
ryan: Nice — that lines up with kernel selection being the trigger.

sasha: Action items: 
- instrument kernel selection metrics (per-layer kernel id, reason code) — sasha/nidhi
- add gating to smoothing so it doesn't cross threshold causing kernel type flips in canary — omar/liam
- adjust batching heuristics to be robust to per-layer latency variance (increase preemption window & small-batch coalescing) — ryan
- run large sweep across representative workloads (long-chat, short-turn, embedding bursts) before re-enabling smoothing — eng-runtime team

omar: Agree. Also want a follow-up hypothesis test: run a calibration sensitivity matrix (grid over clip thresholds x smoothing alpha) and measure kernel-switch count + kv-mem delta. If kernel-switch count correlates with perf regressions we'll block smoothing until mitigations are in place.

jane: Thanks all. Filing a short incident note and tagging product/ops. We avoided user impact by rolling the canary back quickly. :relieved:

ryan: I'll own the sweep. Sharing preliminary run results by EOD tomorrow.

sasha: Adding dashboards for kernel-switch and kv-resident-by-layer to console.

omar: Closing loop for now. If anyone sees similar in other regions ping here.
